correctness.rationale: The pure-inclusion poset has ranks 0,1,2,3 for empty, points, lines and plane. The source proves that pair profiles consisting of ranks, containment/equality and same-rank line-parallelism/intersection have uniform one-element extension support in all affine planes of order q>=3: exactly 148 ordered profile triples across 21 anchored profiles, versus 144 at q=2. Incidence geometry gives q-2 parallel lines not through an external point and q(q-2) points outside a pair of disjoint lines, precisely the q=2 exceptions. These counts depend only on axioms, including non-Desarguesian cases, supporting arbitrary-length three-pebble back-and-forth for q>=3. Independently implemented exact noncounting FO³ type refinement on complete AG(2,2) and AG(2,3) pure inclusion posets: for unassigned triples, equality at ranks 0,1,2,3 and first inequality at rank 4; type counts 45,192,245,367,444. The finite logic refinement is exhaustive for those two models, not a general finite-sample extrapolation; the all-plane extension lemma transfers order-3 theory to all q>=3. The proof also argues two-pebble collapse across all q and rank<=3 agreement with unrestricted pebbles by forgetting profiles unobservable at low quantifier rank. Smallest representatives have 12 (q2) and 23 (q3) flats.
